transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Sharma (Redwood SE), Carlos Ruiz (CTO, Aurora Medical), Maya Patel (ML Engineer), Liam O'Connor (Head of Platform)
Links shared: Model catalog deck (slides), Benchmark spreadsheet: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/aurora, Security docs: https://redwood.example.com/security/aurora, Demo console recording (will share)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, appreciate you taking the time. quick agenda — walk through our model catalog in the console, show how you pick open models, look at perf/quality benchmarks, and then talk about compatibility with your infra. Priya will run the console demo.
[00:29] Carlos: great, thanks. high level, we have two main use cases — clinical note summarization (high quality, lower throughput) and triage routing (low latency, higher throughput). also some security constraints — data residency and KMS.
[01:05] Priya: perfect, yeah that maps well. starting in the Redwood Console -> Model Catalog. you can filter by license, size, quantization options, and our verified perf profiles. so for open models we show Llama-2 variants, Mistral, MPT, Falcon, plus community forks. note we surface quantized variants like -q4f32 and q8_0 which change memory and perf.
[01:42] Maya: quick q — do you include evaluation benchmarks for both quality and latency? we need to know p50/p95 and also rouge/chrF or custom evals.
[02:10] Priya: yes, each model profile includes a benchmark tab with throughput (tokens/sec), latency p50/p95 for typical seq lengths, and a small quality overlay — and you can upload your own eval prompts to run a private eval. our default benchmarks are on an H100 and an A100 cluster for reference; we also provide estimates for Dedicated SKUs like NVIDIA L4/A10G for cost forecasting.
[03:00] Jordan: and to be clear, benchmarks in the catalog are indicative; for mission critical workloads we recommend running the benchmark harness we share (sheet + scripts) against your prompts. priya, show the compatibility matrix.
[03:28] Priya: right — compatibility matrix. this shows which model variants are supported on which runtimes and which quantizations work with KV cache, streaming, and function calling. e.g., some community q4 variants don't support efficient kv-cache, so they degrade generation latency for chat-like workloads.
[04:05] Liam: interesting, we rely heavily on kv-cache for our triage flows. if kv-cache isn't efficient that will break our p95. which models would you recommend for low-latency prefix/caching?
[04:32] Priya: for cache-friendly low-latency we typically recommend medium-size quantized Llama-2 or Mistral 7B-q4 variants on H100 or A100 with continuous batching disabled for strict latency SLOs. for higher throughput we suggest batching on Dedicated L4 pools.
[05:00] Carlos: ok but cost is a concern — how much cheaper would a q4 quantized model be vs the FP16 hosted variant?
[05:20] Priya: ballpark — q4 can reduce memory footprint by ~60-70% and token cost roughly 2-3x depending on batching and KV cache hit rates. Redwood Optimize also gives recommendations for batch size and cache TTL to hit target cost/latency tradeoffs.
[06:00] [small cross talk] Maya: and for the summarization pipeline we need best-in-class quality. are there side-by-side quality benchmarks?
[06:25] Priya: yes, the catalog supports side-by-side evals; we have curated eval suites for summarization, instruction-following, and clinical extraction. you can also attach your own scoring script to compare rouge/f1. for Aurora, Jordan suggested we run your 1000-sample clinical prompt set.
[07:02] Jordan: yeah, that would help — we'll run models Llama-2-13B, Mistral-7B-Instruct, and Falcon-40B-open for quality and latency; start with hosted quick tests then if promising we move to Dedicated pilot.
[07:35] Carlos: Falcon-40B seems heavy — any recommendations on a memory-limited environment?
[07:50] Priya: for 40B you need a lot of memory; we provide quantized 40B options but there are tradeoffs in quality. many teams pick 13B quantized models for a sweet spot between quality and cost for summarization.
[08:15] Maya: can you explain the matrix row where it says "streaming unsupported" on some quant variants? we've seen timeouts when streaming partial tokens in certain setups.
[08:40] Priya: yeah, older community kernels sometimes don't support token streaming; our runtime flags that in compatibility. if streaming is required we pick a variant with proven streaming support — the catalog shows a compatibility badge.
[09:05] Jordan: quick demo — I'm switching to the benchmark tab for Llama-2-13B-q4f32. you can see token/sec numbers, cost per 1k tokens estimate, p50/p95 for 32/128 tokens. there are also raw traces you can download. link in chat.
[09:40] [screen share noise] Priya: also note the model card includes recommended hardware — e.g., run q4f32 on H100 for best latency; for Dedicated we suggest an L4 pool with >n cores/ram depending on batch size.
[10:10] Liam: about Dedicated — if we reserve capacity, can we control eviction and fallback? if Dedicated capacity is saturated, what happens for real-time triage?
[10:32] Jordan: Redwood can route per-policy — you can set primary Dedicated pool with fallback to hosted (lower-priority) or alternative model (lower-cost variant). routing policies and rate limits are configurable in the Console.
[11:00] Maya: security question — do you store prompts or customer data by default? we need to know retention and KMS for encryption.
[11:20] Jordan: hosted default is ephemeral caching for performance and telemetry; for enterprise we have options: disable retention, bring-your-own-key (KMS/HSM), and Private deployment where control plane is customer-managed. we'll share SOC2 docs.
[12:00] Priya: back to perf — for triage we ran a small benchmark on our side: Llama-2-7B-q4 on A100, p95 ~ 120ms for 32 tokens in isolated tests; p95 increases under contention — which is why KV cache and batching matter.
[12:40] Carlos: is Redwood Optimize something we run, or is it built-in?
[12:55] Priya: Redwood Optimize is part of the Console — it analyzes request patterns and suggests batching/cache/quantization changes. you can apply suggestions automatically or export recommended configs. also gives projected cost savings.
[13:30] [background noise] Maya: do you support on-prem/offline air-gapped deployments? we have some patients data that can't leave net.
[13:50] Jordan: yes, Private deployments (VPC or on-prem) are supported; we provide a package and a private control plane option. there is an enterprise fee and an additional ops runbook.
[14:15] Liam: network topology — can we peer our VPC to Redwood Dedicated? and how do healthchecks and logging work?
[14:32] Priya: you can peering or direct connect; logs are pushed to customer SIEM and we provide audit logs and RBAC. healthchecks are configurable and Redwood console surfaces per-route latency and error traces.
[15:05] Jordan: quick detour — let's look at compatibility rows for the models you care about. Maya, you mentioned triage and summarization. Priya, filter catalog for summarization-optimized models.
[15:35] Priya: filtering... showing Llama-2-13B variants, Mistral-7B-Instruct, and a couple of Falcon forks. see column for "kv-cache support" — Mistral-7B-q4f32 shows full support. Llama-2-13B-q4 has partial support depending on kernel.
[16:10] Carlos: ok great. can the Console run a one-click eval against our prompt set in a sandboxed way? we need to ensure PHI isn't stored.
[16:32] Priya: yes — there's a private eval mode that uses ephemeral instances and doesn't persist logs; results are returned to you and we can wipe traces on completion. you'll need to sign the DPA addendum for PHI workflows; we'll include that in the security docs.
[17:05] Maya: what about streaming + function calling with these models, we do a lot of structured outputs for triage.
[17:25] Priya: function calling is supported on most variants; the compatibility matrix shows support for structured outputs and streaming. we flag models where certain features are experimental.
[18:00] Jordan: pricing question — for hosted, is it per-token and then we have the Dedicated commit? how do you price quantized variants?
[18:20] Priya: hosted is per-token; quantized variants often have lower per-token price in the catalog because they use less GPU time. Dedicated is commit-based — you reserve pool units and get lower token costs and consistent latency. we can model a cost comparison in the spreadsheet.
[19:00] Maya: can we get raw latency traces? we'd like to feed them into our SRE tools for alerting thresholds.
[19:20] Jordan: yes, we'll share downloadable traces and structured JSON traces for integration. action item for us to upload sample traces from the benchmark run.
[20:00] [pause] Liam: on the compatibility doc there's a note about "unlikely to support kv for q8 variants" — is that because of kernel differences?
[20:18] Priya: exactly — some q8 kernels don't integrate with our fast KV cache path, so they fall back to less efficient memory access patterns. that shows up as higher p95 in our lab traces.
[21:00] Carlos: what's the recommended next step? pilot? POC?
[21:18] Jordan: recommended path for Aurora: 1) quick hosted eval (we run your 1k prompts on hosted catalog models) to get quality/latency baseline; 2) if okay, spin up a short Dedicated pilot for triage with an L4 pool to verify p95 under load; 3) if PHI concerns, schedule Private deep-dive.
[22:00] Maya: timeline — we want results within two weeks. is that feasible?
[22:20] Jordan: yes — hosted eval can be done within 3-5 business days after we get prompts; Dedicated pilot setup takes ~1-2 weeks depending on commit.
[23:00] Priya: follow-ups: I'll start the first run on Llama-2-13B-q4 and Mistral-7B-Instruct as soon as we get your prompt set and account creds.
[23:30] Carlos: for the quality eval, can you include a diff/annotation view so we can see where outputs diverge?
[23:50] Priya: yep, side-by-side diff and token-level alignment; we'll include rouge/f1 and example outputs in the sheet.
[24:20] [ambient sounds] Maya: one more infra question — will the Dedicated pool autoscale? we want to handle spikes during clinic hours.
[24:40] Jordan: Dedicated supports autoscaling policies and burst capacity; policies are configurable in the Console and we can set soft/hard caps to control cost.
[25:10] Liam: do you offer SLA on latency or just uptime?
[25:30] Jordan: SLA focuses on uptime for Dedicated; latency SLAs are available as enterprise add-on depending on reserved capacity and agreed SLOs.
[26:05] Maya: any gotchas with our current stack — we run on AWS, EKS, and use KMS and private subnets.
[26:30] Priya: that's a supported pattern — Private or Dedicated with VPC peering is common. for KMS you can bring keys; we have examples in the security doc.
[27:00] [typing noise] Jordan: summarizing next steps — Jordan to send pricing and model-cost estimates; Priya to run hosted benchmarks when Maya shares prompt set; Redwood to share compatibility matrix and raw traces; schedule Private deep-dive pending PHI requirements.
[27:35] Carlos: sounds good. can you include an explicit list of recommended models for our two workloads?
[27:50] Priya: yes — we'll recommend 3x models per workload (quality-weighted, cost-weighted, latency-weighted). for summarization: Llama-2-13B-q4, Mistral-7B-Instruct, Llama-2-70B (FP16 if you want top quality). for triage: Llama-2-7B-q4, Mistral-7B-q4 low-latency, and a Falcon-7B fork for throughput test.
[29:00] Maya: ok great, please include the exact Docker/base image or runtime kernel tags — we need to match our on-prem tests.
[29:22] Priya: noted — we'll include kernel & runtime tags in the compatibility matrix.
[30:00] Jordan: last minute security note — if you plan to run tests with PHI, we'll need the DPA and for Redwood to sign BAAs; otherwise run sanitized data.
[30:25] Carlos: we'll sanitize for the first run.
[30:40] Maya: any limitations for function calling when using quantized models? we rely on structured JSON outputs.
[31:00] Priya: function calling works on most quantized variants but some heavy quantization can cause tokenization differences; we'll flag that. the compatibility matrix shows "function-calling: supported/experimental" per variant.
[31:40] Jordan: closing — I'll recap in the follow-up email with links and timelines.
[32:00] [wrap up chatter] Jordan: thanks everyone, talk soon.

Recap / Next Steps (verbatim):
